oewn-05659244-n.learner: the ability to hold on to past experience and bring it back to mind
examples: Elizabeth was pleased to find his memory so exact.
Her memory for names and faces was very good.
I could forgive him anything and everything, rather than his disappointing the hopes and disgracing the memory of his father.
The smell of the sea brought back a memory of that summer.

oewn-05768199-n.learner: the work the mind does when it brings back past experience
examples: He played the whole tune from memory, with no music in front of him.

oewn-02576745-a.learner: not wanting to do something and refusing to do it
examples: Unwilling as she was to admit an idea so destructive to Jane's happiness, she could not prevent its frequently recurring.
She was not so unwilling to comply with their brother's proposal.

oewn-02532301-s.learner: happening even though the person does not want it to
examples: An unwilling smile crossed his face as he listened.
He gave an unwilling nod and followed the others out.

oewn-00164857-a.learner: giving care or attention to someone or something, often shown with the word ‘to’
examples: Lady Catherine is a very respectable, sensible woman, indeed, and a most attentive neighbour.
His behaviour was attentive and kind to the utmost.

oewn-01198026-a.learner: taking notice of something and giving it close, careful thought
examples: The class stayed attentive while the teacher worked through the problem.

oewn-13880467-n.learner: the state of being exactly against something
examples: She said nothing to the contrary, so we went ahead with the plan.

oewn-13880801-n.learner: a link between two things in which each is the direct opposite of the other
examples: On the contrary, she was as much disposed to complain of it as her husband.
On the contrary, there is something pleasing about his mouth when he speaks.

oewn-13805633-n.learner: in logic, one of two statements that cannot both be true, though both of them can be false
examples: ‘Every swan is white’ and ‘no swan is white’ are contraries: both cannot be true, but both may be false.

oewn-02759740-v.learner: to be set against something, or to say that you do not approve of it
examples: They pronounced her to be a sweet girl, and one whom they should not object to know more of.
Lady Catherine very much objected to be kept waiting for her dinner.

oewn-00809123-v.learner: to speak up with an objection, a protest, or a criticism, or to say that you disagree
examples: She objected that the rules had never been explained to anyone.
He objected loudly as soon as the plan was read out.

oewn-00107917-r.learner: to a degree that is great enough for people to notice it
examples: With them he is remarkably agreeable.
Even Mr. Darcy acknowledged that the partridges were remarkably well done.

oewn-00456645-r.learner: in a way that stands out clearly and cannot be mistaken
examples: He failed remarkably to keep his word, and no one could pretend otherwise.

oewn-00905339-v.learner: to stop blaming someone, or to pardon them for what they did
examples: I could easily forgive his pride, if he had not mortified mine.
He has heartily forgiven me now.

oewn-02570341-v.learner: to free someone from having to pay what they owe
examples: The lender agreed to forgive the rest of the debt.

oewn-03773881-n.learner: a hole or set of tunnels dug in the ground to take out ores and minerals
examples: The men went down into the coal mine before it was light.

oewn-03773667-n.learner: a bomb that goes off when something touches it, made to destroy vehicles or ships or to kill or wound people
examples: The ship struck a mine just outside the harbour and sank.

oewn-06661469-n.learner: a fact or a claim that you put forward to show that something is true
examples: The arguments with which you have supported this extraordinary application have been as frivolous as the application was ill-judged.

oewn-07197811-n.learner: a quarrel in speech between people who strongly disagree
examples: Arguments are too much like disputes.
She continued to declare that she would; and the argument ended only with the visit.

oewn-07155686-n.learner: a talk in which reasons are given for and against an idea or a plan
examples: Let us hear all the particulars, for that will have more weight in the argument, Miss Bennet, than you may be aware of.

oewn-01131763-v.learner: to watch over someone or something and keep them safe from danger or harm
examples: Young women should always be properly guarded and attended, according to their situation in life.
A big dog guarded the sheep through the night.

oewn-02461453-v.learner: to keep watch over someone or something
examples: Two soldiers guarded the prisoners all the way to the town.

oewn-02605875-v.learner: to take care beforehand so that something you do not want does not happen
examples: We must guard against making the same mistake a second time.
